source_text:
definition is also considered a declaration. We find this terminology to be most unfortunate, as it doesn’t reflect the
important notion that many definitions are also self-declaring (e.g., int x;), while others, such as those residing
outside of the namespace in which they must also be separately declared (e.g., int ns::x;), are not. Throughout this
book, when we use the term definition only, we mean that the definition itself is explicitly not self-declaring.
